class.name: DampedSpringParameters
class.brief_description: Tuning (response time and damping) for a damped spring, shared by [DampedSpring], [DampedSpring2D], and [DampedSpring3D].
class.description:
A [Resource] holding how quickly a damped spring responds ([member time]) and whether it overshoots, settles cleanly, or lags behind ([member damping]). It doesn't hold any spring state itself. That state lives on [DampedSpring], [DampedSpring2D], or [DampedSpring3D], which read a [DampedSpringParameters] resource every time their [code]update()[/code] method is called.
Because it's a plain, stateless [Resource], one [DampedSpringParameters] can be shared by many spring instances that should all move with the same feel -- for example, every draggable UI element in a menu using the same "snappy" tuning.

method.name: setup
method.description: Sets [member time] and [member damping] together and recomputes the spring's internal coefficients once. Prefer this over setting [member time] and [member damping] separately when changing both, since each of those setters also triggers its own recomputation.

members.member: How overdamped or underdamped the spring is, clamped to the range [code][-0.9, 0.9][/code]. [code]0.0[/code] is critically damped: the fastest response that doesn't overshoot the target. Positive values are increasingly overdamped, which gives a sluggish feeling (good for camera movement). Negative values are increasingly underdamped: the spring oscillates and overshoots its target, good for things like drone following.

Read-only. The [code]c[/code] coefficient (mass = 1) derived from [member time] and [member damping] by [method setup], for the formula [code]F = -k*(value - target) - c*velocity[/code]. Recomputed automatically whenever [member time] or [member damping] changes; exposed so it can be read directly, e.g. to pass into [method DampedSpring.update_constants] or blend it by hand.

Read-only. The [code]k[/code] coefficient (mass = 1) derived from [member time] and [member damping] by [method setup], for the formula [code]F = -k*(value - target) - c*velocity[/code]. Recomputed automatically whenever [member time] or [member damping] changes; exposed so it can be read directly, e.g. to pass into [method DampedSpring.update_constants] or blend it by hand.

How long the spring takes to respond, in seconds. Its precise meaning depends on [member damping]: for a critically damped or overdamped spring ([member damping] [code]>= 0.0[/code]), it's an approximate duration for the spring to settle near its target; for an underdamped spring ([member damping] [code]< 0.0[/code]), it's the time until the spring reaches its first peak overshoot. Clamped to a small positive minimum.
